text: Alice Ramos: Quick Q: .NET HttpClient + Basic auth mismatch. We moved a CI runner to pull the API key from Parameter Store and our requests to /v1/chat started returning 401s. When I dump the outgoing header on the runner it shows `Authorization: Basic <token>` and it looks like what Postman sends, but server rejects. Code is: `client.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Basic", apiKeyBase64);` How should we be generating the base64? Do we need to include the trailing colon? Any common gotchas with PowerShell/AWS CLI adding quotes or CRLFs?
text_2: Ben Cho: Basic == base64 of `username:password`. For API keys we expect `base64(apiKey + ':')`. HttpClient won't alter the Authorization header for you. Common culprits: trailing newline, surrounding quotes, or the secret being JSON-encoded. Try in C#: `Convert.ToBase64String(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(apiKey + ":"))`. In bash: `echo -n 'mykey:' | base64` (note `-n`).

Maria Patel: Also watch Windows CRLF and PowerShell `echo` behavior. `echo` adds `
` on PS. When reading from files use `Get-Content -Raw` and `.Trim()`; in PS you can `Get-Content secret.txt -Raw | Trim` (or `-NoNewline` when writing). If using SSM/SecretsManager double-check the stored value doesn't include extra quotes (some scripts insert `"` unintentionally).

text_5: Alice Ramos: Found it — the value in Parameter Store had surrounding quotes because the original deploy script did `--string-value '"$KEY"'`. The env var had literal `"` around it, so our base64 included quotes and failed. Trimmed quotes and used `Convert.ToBase64String(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(envApiKey + ":"))` and requests are now succeeding. Will open a docs PR with a C# snippet + troubleshooting note.
text_6: Ben Cho: :thumbsup: please link the PR when it's up. Also consider a small SDK test that asserts the header matches `^Basic [A-Za-z0-9+/]+=*$` to catch obvious mis-encodings.
